text:
sophia: Quick sync — we need a compact recruitment checklist + success criteria for the new "engagement portfolio" beta cohort. Trying to lock this down for the partner ops doc by EOD. TL;DR: who we recruit, what feedback signals we need, and immediate go/no-go gates.

kevin_pm: +1. Can we standardize to a single intake form and a short triage call? Keeps ops overhead low.

tom_cs: We should require at least one integration signal (e.g., built PoC using Redwood API) — that weeds out low-value partners. Also ask for expected QPS and primary SLA needs.

anna_eng: For acceptance/gates, propose: 1) integration PoC, 2) 2 core use-cases with sample prompts, 3) owner commitment for 4-week feedback cadence. If any missing, mark as "exploratory" not full beta.

maya_research: Add a small eval suite we run pre-onboard: 10 prompts that cover latency, hallucination, and API error handling. We'll baseline and attach to the partner.

kevin_pm: Nice. What are the measurable feedback signals? Response rate to weekly check-ins? Usage growth? Qualitative NPS? Need both ops-friendly metrics and product-facing signals.

tom_cs: Recommended signals: weekly active users (or API calls per day), monthly retention on test flows, two prioritized bug/regression reports per partner, and a qualitative health score from CS call (1-5).

samir_ops: Ops constraints: limit initial cohort to 8 partners to keep dedicated onboarding bandwidth. Also require a deployment window preference and a data policy sign-off (privacy + logs retention).

eng-ops-bot: reminder: onboarding seats available this sprint: 6. Please update the intake repo.

sophia: Ok combining: intake form + triage call + PoC + 2 use-cases + eval suite + owner commit + metrics list. Can someone sketch the minimal intake form fields?

kevin_pm: Minimal fields: company, primary contact, product use-case, expected monthly tokens/QPS, compliance needs (SOC2/PII), desired start date, success criteria (partner), any blocked infra reqs.

maya_research: Add: sample prompts + golden outputs (if applicable) and any existing evals they run. Helps us map to our eval suite.

anna_eng: Also capture model/quantization preferences and whether they need private/dedicated. That's a big routing decision.

tom_cs: One more: a short "value statement" — what's their core success metric (e.g., reduce support deflection 20%). That helps prioritize who gets seats.

samir_ops: About go/no-go: propose a rapid 7-day probation after PoC. If the partner can't provide the PoC or misses 2 check-ins, we escalate to exploratory and free the seat. Thoughts?

kevin_pm: Agree. Escalation path: exploratory -> mentoring slot -> archival. But keep one exception window for high strategic partners (sales to sign off).

sophia: This reads well. Next steps: kevin will draft the intake form, maya will author the 10-prompt eval, tom will draft the CS scoring rubric, anna will write the engineering onboarding checklist, samir will confirm seat availability and the data sign-off template. Can we aim for drafts by tomorrow noon?

kevin_pm: I'll have the intake draft by 11am.

maya_research: Eval draft by 11:30.

tom_cs: Rubric done by noon.

anna_eng: Onboarding checklist by noon.

samir_ops: I'll confirm seats + data policy template by noon.

sophia: Perfect. I'll collate into the product doc and add acceptance gates. Final ask: let's keep public-facing partner language short — 3 bullet points: what to expect, time commitment, and success criteria.

kevin_pm: Agreed. Short, clear.

tom_cs: +1 :thumbsup:

eng-ops-bot: task created: /tasks/ENGAGEMENT-BETA-INTAKE assigned to kevin_pm, tom_cs, maya_research, anna_eng, samir_ops — due 12:00 tomorrow.

sophia: Thanks team — talk in the async doc after you post drafts. If anything blocks, ping me directly."
